To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the majority of rheumatology specialists in India (n= 150) were able to provide care during the covid  19 pandemic; 2) the majority of patients with RDs were able to access care during the covid pandemic; 3) the majority of the patients with RDs who were able to access rheumatology care were able to do so in-person; and 4) the majority of respondents were not able to provide care to all their patients with RDs

rheumatology specialists in India have experienced a significant decrease in the number of patients presenting for care, a decrease in the number and type of referrals, and a reduction in the number of new patients.
the pandemic has had a significant influence on the practice of rheumatologists and the treatment of RDs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the management of RDs during the covid 10 pandemic in India.
the impact of the pandemic on the management of RDs, the impact of RDs on patients with covid 19, and the impact of covid 19 on RDs.
the following: (1) the prevalence of RDs in patients with covid 19; (2) the effect of RDs on the clinical manifestations of covid 19; and (3) the effect of covid 19 on the management of RDs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there was no significant change in the clinical management of RDs during the covid 10 pandemic.
there are no conclusive statements, but rather a lot of questions that need to be answered in future studies.
there is a need to develop and implement a comprehensive and detailed strategy that would be applicable to the entire country and would be based on the current situation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are all in this together.
the majority of rheumatology practices in India are not fully prepared to deal with the pandemic, and the majority of the respondents were not confident of their preparedness.
there is a need to develop a national consensus for managing RDs in the time of a pandemic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RD patients are at risk of being infected with covid 19 and that they have a higher risk of severe covid 19 disease and death than the general population.
rheumatology practitioners in India are well equipped to handle the covid 19 situation.
RDs are not a priority for the healthcare system in India during this pandemic.
